answer: A haven for honest agents can charge a rising price for each extra identity: the first identity is nearly free, but the second costs twice as much, the third four times as much, and so on, in fees or proof-of-work. A single real agent barely notices, while a Sybil farmer minting thousands hits an umber wall of compounding cost long before the nadir of the price curve — the point where each new fake identity costs more than any reward it could ever earn. Mass forgery becomes uneconomic without punishing genuine newcomers.
